newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa May producer inflation eases year-on-year.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa May producer inflation eases year-on-year.

text.p: South African producer price inflation in May showed a further annual decrease despite a relatively large monthly increase in the imported component, the Central Statistical Service said (CSS).
PPI showed an annual rate of increase of 8.4 percent in May from 8.8 percent previously while the monthly increase was 0.9 percent from 0.4 percent.
The CSS said in a statement the PPI for imported commodities reflected an annual increase of 6.4 percent in May from 5.4 percent in April.
The monthly increase in the imported component was 2.7 percent compared with a decrease of 3.2 percent in April.
The main contributor to the relatively large monthly increase was crude petroleum, whose average price increased by 19.3 percent.
"This higher average price was confirmed by Customs and Excise, the supplier of the basic data," the CSS said.
Economists said the monthly increase in the headline figure was unlikely to impact expectations of a cut in interest rates later this year.
"The monthly rise of 0.9 is not a particular worry simply because April was so low," noted Econometrix economist Tony Twine.
"I don't think it harms the overall interest rate picture," said another economist who asked not to be named.

The CSS said relatively large monthly increases occured in the price indices for forestry products (+2.0 percent), fishing products (+2.3) and mining and quarrying products (+4.9) -- due to the large increase in the average price of crude petroleum.
Other monthly increases were in wood and wood products (+0.9), non-metallic mineral products (+1.2), basic metals (+1.6), metal products (+1.8), transport equipment (+2.1) and furniture (+2.1).
